# Job-posting platforms

<!-- Generated by scripts/platform_catalog.py from data/platforms.json. Edit the JSON, then run: python3 scripts/platform_catalog.py --write [--sweep <a find_site_boards.py results file>]. selftest's check_every_reader_has_a_platform_entry holds the two together. -->

One entry for every job-posting platform SLED JOBS reads or meets: every reader in ats.FETCHERS (html, the page scan, among them), the platforms researched live on 2026-11-19..21 that have no reader, and every vendor the finder's ELSEWHERE list recognises. Each entry says how a company's site shows the platform, how it publishes its postings, what robots.txt allows, where a board names its employer, its quirks, and which functions read and probe it.

Written from the code (the readers in scripts/ats.py, the finder's patterns in scripts/find_site_boards.py, the probes in scripts/verify_boards.py, build_board.board_url) and from the research of 2026-11-19..21, whose evidence sat in scratch files that are not kept. Where the research and the code disagree, the code is what runs, and the entry's notes say so. Nothing is guessed: what the sources do not settle says unknown.

How a platform is met. find_site_boards.py reads a company's own website: an address in one of its board patterns is a candidate, naming a board a reader takes; an address on a platform nothing reads, or a form of one we read that names no board, is tallied under elsewhere (ELSEWHERE, with TENANT_FORMS and \_NO_BOARD_IN_IT saying which forms belong to which platform). The reader in ats.FETCHERS reads the board. verify_boards.board_says asks the board whose it is, and proven() decides whether the name it states is the company's. wire_found.py wires a found board only when both checks agree (the owner's rule, 2026-11-18).

measured_on lists the days the code or the research records a live measurement; a window (day..day) is a day within it that the research does not narrow down; unknown is none recorded. A form is a finder vendor id that belongs to the platform and names no board the wiring door can use.

50 platforms: 28 read, 1 build, 3 skip, 18 seen.

| Status | Means |
|---|---|
| **read** | A reader exists in ats.FETCHERS; the nightly crawl reads boards of this type. |
| **build** | Researched; worth a reader; not built yet. |
| **maybe** | Researched; worth a reader only on the conditions the entry names. |
| **skip** | Researched; cannot or should not be read, for the reason the entry gives. |
| **seen** | The finder recognises it (find_site_boards.ELSEWHERE); not researched yet. |

## Platforms we read

### A careers page (html)

`html` · **read** · reader `ats.fetch_html` · no identity probe · measured 2026-08-23, 2026-11-18

**How to spot it.** Any careers page with no board behind it that another reader takes. Discovery also files several vendors' addresses as html (discover_ats.MARKERS): ADP's recruitment.html page, paycomonline.net's jobs?clientkey= list, jobs.jobvite.com/\<slug>, \<label>.teamtailor.com, applicantpro.com, clearcompany.com, isolvedhire.com, dayforcehcm.com, recruiting.ultipro.com/\<TENANT>, pinpointhq.com, taleo.net, avature.net, csod.com and careers.hibob.com.

**How it publishes.** The page itself. refresh.py's reader, fetch_html, returns one pseudo-row carrying the page's visible text for the classifier (a page under 400 characters raises: likely JavaScript-rendered). build_board reads the same page with fetch_html_titles, which counts a link only when its address looks like a job's and its text like a title, needs two, deduplicates on the link, and takes schema.org JobPosting blocks already in the page; a shell falls back to a headless browser (render_fetch.fetch_rendered) within the nightly render budget.

**Public link** (`build_board.board_url`). The ref (the page's address).

**robots.txt.** Asked at every hop (ats.\_page). A rendered read walks the address's redirects with ats.resolve first and keeps nothing from a page whose final address is refused.

**Where it names its employer.** Names nobody: board_says' html branch records the page's own host and counts its titles ('html board: the page's own host'), and html is not in NAMES_ITS_EMPLOYER, so an html board can never pass proven().

**Quirks.**

- A page scan never proves absence: an unreadable page is Unknown, never None found.
- html does not mean unread: on 2026-11-18, 114 such pages put 1,357 postings on the board every night.
- A page-scan verdict read off another company's careers page is downgraded to Unknown (refresh.\_someone_elses_site).
- A commented-out job is not an opening: comments are stripped before the scan (Pantonium's three commented-out Sales Director rows had published a 'Yes').

### ADP Workforce Now

`adp` · **read** · reader `ats.fetch_adp` · no identity probe · measured 2026-09-02

**How to spot it.** The careers page a person opens, workforcenow.adp.com/mascsr/default/mdf/recruitment/recruitment.html?cid=\<uuid>[&ccId=\<n>\_\<n>], or the API address that page calls (find_site_boards' own patterns). The cid is the ref, followed by '|\<ccId>' only when the link names a career centre other than ADP's default. Hint: workforcenow.adp.com. Nothing guesses a cid: it comes from a link the company published.

**Forms the finder tallies apart** (`find_site_boards.ELSEWHERE`):

- `adp-other`: An address on workforcenow, myjobs or recruiting.adp.com that names no cid.

**How it publishes.** A public JSON API, one GET: https://workforcenow.adp.com/mascsr/default/careercenter/public/events/staffing/v1/job-requisitions?cid=\<cid>&ccId=\<ccId>&lang=en_US&locale=en_US -> jobRequisitions[] with requisitionTitle, requisitionLocations[].nameCode.shortName, itemID and postDate. The careers page itself is a \~5 KB shell that draws nothing until its script asks that API. The reader makes one request and does not page.

**Public link** (`build_board.board_url`). None of its own: board_url links the company's website.

**robots.txt.** Not asked by the reader: it reads ADP's JSON API through ats.\_get, which the owner's ruling of 2026-10-09 exempts as an interface published for programs. Not measured.

**Where it names its employer.** No identity probe: verify_boards.board_says answers 'no identity probe written for adp', so no ADP board can pass proven().

**Quirks.**

- Verified 2026-09-02 against Zenner USA (11 requisitions), with a cid read off the company's own careers page.
- Most portals answer on ADP's default ccId (19000101_000001); the few that need another carry it in the ref.
- The location is ADP's label, a site name then a place ('Minol - Addison, TX'), and the reader keeps the place. The address block beside it was empty on every row seen.
- discover_ats.MARKERS still files the recruitment.html address as type html, which reads as a JavaScript shell ('page too small'); ten companies sat in the discovery log that way when the reader was written.

### ApplicantPro (isolved)

`applicantpro` · **read** · researched as build · reader `ats.fetch_applicantpro` · identity probe `verify_boards._applicantpro` · measured 2026-11-19, 2026-11-21

**How to spot it.** \<label>.applicantpro.com or \<label>.isolvedhire.com (one platform on two root domains, run by isolved) in an href, a src, an iframe or frame, or a redirect (find_site_boards; 'www' and the vendor's own labels skipped). The whole tenant host is the ref: the label alone does not say which domain, and it is not the company's name ('casellejobs'). Hints: applicantpro.com, isolvedhire.com.

**Forms the finder tallies apart** (`find_site_boards.ELSEWHERE`):

- `applicantpro-other`: An address on applicantpro.com or isolvedhire.com that names no tenant: the 'Powered by ApplicantPro' link, and the www.applicantpro.com/openings/\<label>/... form a board's own og:url uses, whose label the finder does not read.

**How it publishes.** Two requests a board. The /jobs/ page (https://\<host>/jobs/) names the domain id the list is asked by, in its JobListings componentData (domainId and getParams), and the list is the call that component makes: GET https://\<host>/core/jobs/\<domainId>?getParams=\<the page's getParams, as JSON> -> {success: true, data: {jobs: [...], jobCount}}, each job with title, city, abbreviation (the state), iso3, jobUrl, startDateRef ('Nov 17, 2026'), workplaceType, payType, minSalary, maxSalary, payTypeFrame and payDetails. The ad is each posting's schema.org block (one request a posting, behind FETCH_DETAILS). No paging: jobCount equalled the rows on every board read.

**Public link** (`build_board.board_url`). https://\<host>/jobs/

**robots.txt.** Asked at every hop: read as pages, held to the tenant's host. Measured 2026-11-19..21: every tenant host read, on both root domains, allows /jobs/, /core/jobs/ and the posting pages, and disallows only /admin/, /stats/ and the internal-jobs paths. Genasys's host gave no rules, and its site is disabled.

**Where it names its employer.** The feed names nobody. The /jobs/ page's courierCurrentRouteData states two names: career_site_name, the site the employer set up, and organization_name, the ApplicantPro account behind it. verify_boards.\_applicantpro states both and requires the site's own name, so a sister brand's site on another company's account states two names and goes to the owner's queue: Black Mountain Software's board is on Caselle's account (2026-11-19).

**Quirks.**

- A DISABLED SITE ANSWERS 200: Genasys's /jobs/ lands, on the same host, on /notset.php?...&disabled=1, 'This career site has been disabled'. That is a board that is gone, never one with nothing open.
- min..max is pay only on a 'Salary' or 'Hourly' row whose payDetails names no commission, OTE, bonus or equity: on 'Base + Commission' it runs from the base floor to the OTE ceiling (LYT's Senior AE: 82000-248000 against a stated base of $82k-$124k). The posting page's baseSalary is not taken either, so a figure refused here cannot come back by another door.
- The list call is the board's own front-end endpoint, not a published API, and its bundles are hash-named, so a front-end release can change it. The research found a server-rendered fallback list at /iframe/mobile; the code does not read it.
- startDateRef is read as '%b %d, %Y' (posted_date does not take that form); a city of 'Remote' is a way of working, not a place.
- discover_ats.MARKERS still files \<label>.applicantpro.com and \<label>.isolvedhire.com as type html.

**Notes.**

- The research left it to the owner whether the probe states organization_name beside career_site_name (stating both sends Black Mountain to his queue); the code states both. The code is what runs.

### Ashby

`ashby` · **read** · reader `ats.fetch_ashby` · identity probe `verify_boards.board_says` · measured 2026-08-23

**How to spot it.** jobs.ashbyhq.com/\<slug>, its embed form jobs.ashbyhq.com/embed?org=\<slug>, or the API address api.ashbyhq.com/posting-api/job-board/\<slug> (find_boards.PATTERNS and discover_ats.MARKERS, borrowed by find_site_boards), plus the finder's own form for a board whose name has a space in it, which arrives as %20 and is read whole ('flock safety', not 'flock'). Hint: ashbyhq.com. The slug is kept as the page spelt it.

**How it publishes.** A documented JSON API, one GET for the whole board: https://api.ashbyhq.com/posting-api/job-board/\<slug>?includeCompensation=true -> {jobs: [...]}, each with title, location, jobUrl or applyUrl, descriptionPlain, publishedAt, workplaceType and, with includeCompensation, pay as numbers: the only board here that publishes a pay range as numbers on its list endpoint. No paging.

**Public link** (`build_board.board_url`). https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/\<slug>

**robots.txt.** Not asked by the reader: it reads Ashby's documented feed through ats.\_get (exempt under the owner's ruling of 2026-10-09). The identity probe reads the board's own page, jobs.ashbyhq.com/\<slug>, through verify_boards.\_board_page, robots.txt asked at every hop. What either host's robots.txt says is not recorded.

**Where it names its employer.** The feed names nobody ({jobs, apiVersion}). The board's own page assigns window.\_\_appData, whose organization block carries the display name and the website the employer gave Ashby: verify_boards.board_says reads the feed, then \_ashby_page states organization.name and gives publicWebsite as the site proven() holds to the one on file. A board marked isDemoOrg names nobody. The slug (hostedJobsPageSlug) is never a name: 'snd' is Social News Desk.

**Quirks.**

- workplaceType gives the mode; isRemote is deliberately unused, because False means not remote, not onsite.

### BambooHR

`bamboohr` · **read** · reader `ats.fetch_bamboohr` · identity probe `verify_boards._bamboohr` · measured 2026-08-23

**How to spot it.** \<slug>.bamboohr.com (find_boards.PATTERNS and discover_ats.MARKERS, borrowed by find_site_boards); the slug is lowered. Hint: bamboohr.com.

**How it publishes.** JSON, one GET: https://\<slug>.bamboohr.com/careers/list -> {result: [...], meta}, each opening with jobOpeningName, atsLocation and location parts, and id. The list carries no description: /careers/\<id>/detail carries the description and a compensation field (one request a posting, behind FETCH_DETAILS). No paging.

**Public link** (`build_board.board_url`). https://\<slug>.bamboohr.com/careers

**robots.txt.** Not asked by the reader (ats.\_get, exempt under the owner's ruling of 2026-10-09). The identity probe reads the careers page through verify_boards.\_board_page, robots.txt at every hop. Not measured.

**Where it names its employer.** The list names nobody. The careers page states the name in og:site_name, and NOT in its \<title>, which is the bare word 'BambooHR' on every board: verify_boards.\_bamboohr reads the list for the count, then \_bamboohr_page.

**Quirks.**

- atsLocation is read first: location is {city: null, state: null} on every row of every board checked, while atsLocation holds 'Denver, Colorado, United States' one key over.
- compensation on the detail record was null on every sample on file.
- BambooHR's marketing site is www.bamboohr.com, on the domain its tenants' boards sit under, so the probe holds every hop to the board's own host.

### Breezy HR

`breezy` · **read** · reader `ats.fetch_breezy` · identity probe `verify_boards._breezy` · measured 2026-08-23

**How to spot it.** \<slug>.breezy.hr (find_boards.PATTERNS and discover_ats.MARKERS, borrowed by find_site_boards); the slug is lowered. Hint: breezy.hr.

**How it publishes.** JSON, one GET: https://\<slug>.breezy.hr/json -> a list of positions with name, location.name, url, published_date and pay as text in the list ('$160,000 - $200,000 / year'). The description is only on each posting page's schema.org JobPosting (one request a posting, behind FETCH_DETAILS). No paging.

**Public link** (`build_board.board_url`). https://\<slug>.breezy.hr

**robots.txt.** Not asked for the feed (ats.\_get, exempt under the owner's ruling of 2026-10-09). The posting pages behind FETCH_DETAILS and the probe's fallback page are read as pages, robots.txt at every hop. Not measured.

**Where it names its employer.** Stated in the feed: company.name on every position, never company.friendly_id, which repeats the slug ('vetro-fibermap-inc' where the name is 'VETRO, Inc'). An empty feed ('[]', Polco's) names nobody, so verify_boards.\_breezy falls back to the hosted page's breezy-doc-title meta (\_breezy_page); not its og:title, which is a slogan the employer types ('Join Our Team').

**Quirks.**

- Pay is free in the list; only the description costs a request.

### Comeet (Spark Hire Recruit)

`comeet` · **read** · researched as build · reader `ats.fetch_comeet` · identity probe `verify_boards._comeet` · measured 2026-11-19, 2026-11-21

**How to spot it.** The company's own iframe or API call, which hands its browser the company uid and the public token together (comeet.co/jobs/\<UID>/social?token=..., or .../jobs/\<UID>/\<position UID>/apply?token=..., or comeet.co/careers-api/2.0/company/\<UID>/positions?token=...); a COMEET.init({...}) script, read one key at a time because Cognyte's object is not JSON; or a hosted board, www.comeet.com/jobs/\<slug>/\<UID> (find_site_boards). A uid is two hex digits, a dot and three more ('F2.004'). The ref is '\<UID>|\<TOKEN>' as the company's page gave them, or the hosted board's address. Hint: comeet.

**Forms the finder tallies apart** (`find_site_boards.ELSEWHERE`):

- `comeet-other`: Any other comeet.co or comeet.com address (a terms link on support.comeet.co, a plugin page).
- `comeet-tenant`: A Comeet address naming a company uid with no token to read it by: a doubt beside a board, unless it names the very tenant a board on the page already is.

**How it publishes.** Comeet's careers API, one request a company, the ad on &details=true: GET https://www.comeet.co/careers-api/2.0/company/\<UID>/positions?token=\<TOKEN>&details=true -> an array of positions with name, location (name, city, state, country), workplace_type, url_comeet_hosted_page and details[] (Description, Responsibilities, Requirements, in order). For a hosted-board ref the reader first reads the hosted page's COMPANY_DATA for the token: two requests. No paging.

**Public link** (`build_board.board_url`). A hosted-board ref is linked as it is; a '\<UID>|\<TOKEN>' ref has no page of its own a person can open, the pair is never printed, and board_url links the company's website.

**robots.txt.** Asked at every hop: read as pages, held to the host. Measured 2026-11-19..21: www.comeet.co and www.comeet.com serve the same file, which allows the API, the iframe and the hosted pages and disallows ?src= and utm\_ parameters (among a few others); never add them.

**Where it names its employer.** Stated on every position: company_name. A hosted board's page also states the account's name and the website it gave (COMPANY_DATA.name and website), both held to the record (verify_boards.\_comeet). An empty list names nobody unless the board is a hosted page, which still names itself. The page \<title> is the vendor's ('Spark Hire Recruit Jobs | ...') and is never read.

**Quirks.**

- Never read: the referral bounty (company_referrals_reward, '3000$', is not pay), the apply alias (email), the categories (one named a hiring manager), and location.is_remote, which is true on every Hybrid row.
- No posting date: time_updated is an edit stamp, so posted is None.
- The token is the public one the company's careers page gives every visitor's browser; a stored one stops working if the employer issues a new one.
- WordPress 'Comeet Jobs' plugin sites (Cellebrite's) keep the token on the server and print no uid, token or comeet address: nothing can be lifted from them, and no slug or uid is ever guessed.
- Mostly a platform for Israeli companies: 26 of the 105 rows the research read were US-located.
- The vendor now calls itself Spark Hire Recruit; the hosts are unchanged, and a move to new hosts would break the reader and the finder's patterns.

**Notes.**

- The research said an empty feed needs a fallback to the hosted page, as breezy's probe has; the code names a board through its hosted page only when the ref is that page, so an empty board on file as '\<UID>|\<TOKEN>' names nobody. The code is what runs.

### Gem

`gem` · **read** · reader `ats.fetch_gem` · identity probe `verify_boards._gem` · measured unknown

**How to spot it.** jobs.gem.com/\<slug> (find_site_boards). The slug is never derived from the company id: City Detect's is citydetect. Hint: jobs.gem.com.

**How it publishes.** Every jobs.gem.com page, board and job alike, is the same \~4 KB JavaScript shell with no JobPosting JSON-LD. The shell calls one public GraphQL endpoint that needs no auth, key or Referer: POST https://jobs.gem.com/api/public/graphql/batch, operation JobBoardList, which the reader sends with descriptionHtml added to the board's own query (and once more without it if that field errors). One request.

**Public link** (`build_board.board_url`). https://jobs.gem.com/\<slug>

**robots.txt.** Not asked: a POST (ats.\_post_json). Not measured.

**Where it names its employer.** Stated by the board's own API, in the one call the reader makes: jobBoardExternal.teamDisplayName (verify_boards.\_gem). A slug that does not exist answers jobBoardExternal null and names nobody.

**Quirks.**

- THE DISCRIMINATOR IS jobBoardExternal: a live board with nothing open and a slug that does not exist return a byte-identical empty postings list, and only the board object tells them apart, so a missing board is Unknown, never None found.
- locations[].name never reaches a row: Gem prints team labels there ('City Detect (AL)'), which would read as an Alabama desk.

### Greenhouse

`greenhouse` · **read** · reader `ats.fetch_greenhouse` · identity probe `verify_boards.board_says` · measured 2026-08-23

**How to spot it.** boards.greenhouse.io/\<slug> or job-boards.greenhouse.io/\<slug>, the embed greenhouse.io/embed/job_board[/js]?for=\<slug> and the feed boards-api.greenhouse.io/v1/boards/\<slug> (find_boards.PATTERNS and discover_ats.MARKERS, borrowed by find_site_boards), plus the finder's own forms: the application-form embed greenhouse.io/embed/job_app?for=\<slug> and the older api.greenhouse.io/v1/boards/\<slug>. Hint: greenhouse.io.

**Forms the finder tallies apart** (`find_site_boards.ELSEWHERE`):

- `greenhouse-eu`: A board in Greenhouse's European region (job-boards.eu.greenhouse.io/\<x>). fetch_greenhouse asks the American API only, so it is tallied apart until a reader can ask the European host: handed over as an ordinary ref it would be asked where it does not live, a 404 or another employer's board.
- `greenhouse-shortlink`: A grnh.se short link, which names no board; a redirect that lands on one is walked one hop further, because Greenhouse's next hop is usually the board.

**How it publishes.** A documented JSON API, one GET: https://boards-api.greenhouse.io/v1/boards/\<slug>/jobs?content=true -> {jobs: [...]} with title, location.name, absolute_url, content (the ad, in the same request), first_published and pay_input_ranges. No paging.

**Public link** (`build_board.board_url`). https://job-boards.greenhouse.io/\<slug>

**robots.txt.** Not asked: a documented feed read through ats.\_get (exempt under the owner's ruling of 2026-10-09); the probe reads the same feed. Not measured.

**Where it names its employer.** Stated in the feed: company_name on every job. verify_boards.board_says keeps every distinct name (a parent's hub stamps different names on different jobs) and the apply hosts of the first eight. judge() still reads it with the older substring test, under which a parent passes ('Jacobs' for 'StreetLight Data (Jacobs)'); proven() requires every name to equal the record's.

**Quirks.**

- posted is first_published, never updated_at, which moves on any edit.
- Pay is in cents on some payloads (min_cents, max_cents) and in units on others (min_value, max_value); both are read and neither is assumed.
- Many companies share boards-api.greenhouse.io, so ats' per-host gate holds them HOST_PAUSE (0.5 s) apart.

### Gusto

`gusto` · **read** · reader `ats.fetch_gusto` · identity probe `verify_boards._gusto` · measured unknown

**How to spot it.** jobs.gusto.com/boards/\<name>-\<uuid> (find_site_boards). The segment is never derived from the company id: kaiden-ai's board is kaiden-incorporated-\<uuid>. Hint: jobs.gusto.com.

**Forms the finder tallies apart** (`find_site_boards.ELSEWHERE`):

- `gusto-posting`: A jobs.gusto.com/postings/... link to one job, which names no board; a redirect that lands on one is walked one hop further.

**How it publishes.** Server-rendered HTML with no API, no JSON-LD and no embedded payload: https://jobs.gusto.com/boards/\<segment>, read in five states, each with a positive marker: populated (/postings/ links), empty ('There are no open positions currently', on a page titled 'Careers at X'), closed ('This job board is closed.'), gone (the body says 404) and anything else (Unknown). A paginated board raises rather than report part of itself.

**Public link** (`build_board.board_url`). https://jobs.gusto.com/boards/\<segment>

**robots.txt.** Asked at every hop (ats.\_page). Not measured.

**Where it names its employer.** Only the title pattern 'Careers at X', believed when the page's first heading says the same X (verify_boards.\_gusto). A closed board is titled the bare word 'Careers' and names nobody; the ref's own name segment is never read.

**Quirks.**

- CLOSED IS NOT EMPTY: a closed board means the employer moved (City Detect left Gusto for Gem, and its Gusto board is still live), so it reads Unknown, never a zero.
- Every /postings/ link must be represented, and fewer rows than cards raises: a partial read is never reported as the board.
- A card stating two pay ranges, or an anchor wrapping two headings, raises rather than guess which belongs to which.

### Hirebridge

`hirebridge` · **read** · researched as build · reader `ats.fetch_hirebridge` · identity probe `verify_boards._hirebridge` · measured 2026-11-19, 2026-11-21

**How to spot it.** Any address on recruit., hbapi. or alerts.hirebridge.com carrying cid=\<number> (find_site_boards): an iframe of the career centre (Hirebridge's stock embed, id=HBIFRAME, as on CentralSquare's careers page), a link to the classic /v3/jobs/list.aspx?cid=, a posting, or the job-alerts page. The cid is the ref; there is no name or slug in these addresses. Hint: hirebridge.com.

**How it publishes.** The JSON feed Hirebridge's own career centre calls from every visitor's browser, one GET for the whole board, descriptions included: https://hbapi.hirebridge.com/careercenter/v2/GetJobListings?cid=\<cid>&language=en&addloc=0&startrow=1&endrow=5000. The body is a JSON string holding the JSON array, so it is decoded twice. One feed serves both UI generations (the classic list.aspx tenants and the /v3/CareerCenter/v2 ones). No paging needed: the career centre itself asks 5,000 rows a batch.

**Public link** (`build_board.board_url`). https://recruit.hirebridge.com/v3/jobs/list.aspx?cid=\<cid>

**robots.txt.** Asked at every hop: read as pages, held to the host. Measured 2026-11-19..21: hbapi.hirebridge.com has no robots.txt (404, so no rules); recruit.hirebridge.com disallows only /application, /company, /jobseeker2 and /jobseeker4 (older career-centre forms a reader never needs).

**Where it names its employer.** Stated on every row of the feed: companyname, with companyurl the website the account gave (empty on Tribute's). verify_boards.\_hirebridge reads the same feed, with no extra request, and holds companyurl to the website on file; rows giving two different websites are not stated. An empty feed names nobody: a cid nobody holds answers '[]' too.

**Quirks.**

- THE FEED IS OVER-BROAD: each row's nested joblist carries internal requisition data (notes naming staff, hiring-manager and coordinator ids) and descriptioninternal, the ad meant for internal applicants. The reader copies the public fields by name and nothing else, and hirebridge.com is in ats.NEVER_CACHED, so no raw answer is written to disk.
- An empty feed is a zero only when the classic career centre answers as a live board (titled '\<Name> Career Center'); a dead cid is sent, on the same host, to /v3/Application/AppErrMsg.aspx, titled 'Hirebridge ATS Error'. Anything else is not known, and not a zero.
- addloc=0 matters: without it a job open in three places comes back as three rows with one jid (EAB, 2026-11-21: 93 rows for 42 jobs).
- publicdate is M/D/YYYY and read as such (posted_date refuses to guess an order); never createdate, which is when the requisition was opened.
- location.isremote true means remote; false is not stated (it was false on six of the seven CentralSquare roles whose title says Remote).
- The places are joblocname plus additionalLocations; neither alone is the list.
- The older career-centre forms (/jobseeker2, /jobseeker4) are robots-closed: a cid lifted from such a link is read through the feed.

**Notes.**

- The research said an empty feed should read as an empty board, with gone told from empty in the probe or once when the board is wired; the code's reader asks the classic career centre itself, on every empty read, and raises unless it answers as a live board. The code is what runs.

### iCIMS

`icims` · **read** · reader `ats.fetch_icims` · identity probe `verify_boards._icims` · measured 2026-08-23, 2026-09-01, 2026-10-09

**How to spot it.** \<slug>.icims.com (discover_ats.MARKERS, borrowed by find_site_boards; lowered), or a full portal address on icims.com. Hint: icims.com.

**How it publishes.** A server-rendered portal: the plain address is a \~600-character shell with the list in an iframe, and ?in_iframe=1 returns the real list, https://\<slug>.icims.com/jobs/search?ss=1&in_iframe=1&pr=\<n>. Titles are the iCIMS_Anchor title attribute, '\<req id> - \<title>'. Paged by number (about 20 a page) until a page adds no new link, at most 60 pages, and deduplicated on the link, never the title. The ad is each posting page's schema.org JobPosting (behind FETCH_DETAILS).

**Public link** (`build_board.board_url`). https://\<slug>.icims.com/jobs/search?ss=1; a full-address ref is linked as it is.

**robots.txt.** Asked at every hop (ats.\_page). Measured 2026-10-09: iCIMS portals saying 'Disallow: /' cost Bruker Detection 213 postings and BigBear.ai 64 when the crawler began honouring robots.txt.

**Where it names its employer.** Stated on the board's own first page: iCIMS writes one sentence into the meta description, 'View all current positions at X across all categories and locations.', and X is the ACCOUNT holder (not the \<title>, which employers rewrite). verify_boards.\_icims reads it, and a full-address ref must be on icims.com. The account can be a third party's: Selux's portal says 'Council of Industry'.

**Quirks.**

- The probe reads the first page only (n_is_partial): a board's size comes from the reader, which pages to the end.
- Paged to the end since 2026-09-01: Bruker's portal served nineteen on its first page and twenty after, eleven pages and 204 links; deduplicating on the title had deleted 27 real requisitions.
- An empty portal raises ('no jobs parsed from iCIMS portal'): Unknown, never a zero.
- A Jibe site answers ?in_iframe=1 with a script that bounces back: that is the jibe type, not this one.

### JazzHR

`jazzhr` · **read** · reader `ats.fetch_jazzhr` · identity probe `verify_boards._jazzhr` · measured 2026-08-23, 2026-09-01, 2026-11-18

**How to spot it.** \<slug>.applytojob.com (discover_ats.MARKERS, borrowed by find_site_boards) and the embed script app.jazz.co/widgets/basic/create/\<slug> (the finder's own); lowered. Hints: applytojob.com, jazz.co.

**How it publishes.** A server-rendered list of \<a> job links at https://\<slug>.applytojob.com/apply/. The list page carries only an Organization block; the ad, and a structured baseSalary when the employer set one, are on each posting page (behind FETCH_DETAILS). No paging.

**Public link** (`build_board.board_url`). https://\<slug>.applytojob.com/apply

**robots.txt.** Asked at every hop (ats.\_page). Not measured.

**Where it names its employer.** Stated on the board's own page as a JSON-LD Organization block, with the website the employer typed beside it: verify_boards.\_jazzhr states the name and gives the site to proven(). An inactive board has no block and is titled 'JazzHR - Inactive Career Page', so the name is never read from the title.

**Quirks.**

- A dead or mistyped slug redirects to info.jazzhr.com and on to www.jazzhr.com/job-seekers, a marketing page with an Organization block of its own (measured 2026-11-18): the probe refuses any hop off the board's host.
- A page with no job links raises unless it says it has none ('no open positions' and the like): an unreadable board is not an empty one.
- The title is measured after stripping: JazzHR indents its anchors by 77 characters, and a bound on the raw text kept 2 of 51 real postings (measured across twelve boards, 2026-09-01).

### Jibe (iCIMS Talent Cloud)

`jibe` · **read** · reader `ats.fetch_jibe` · identity probe `verify_boards.board_says` · measured unknown

**How to spot it.** Jibe lives on the company's own careers host and its address names nobody, so find_site_boards spots it by the script host its pages load, jibecdn.com (JIBE_MARK), and takes the host of the page it was seen on as the ref.

**How it publishes.** JSON on the careers host: https://\<careers host>/api/jobs?page=\<n>&limit=100 -> {jobs: [{data: {...}}], totalCount}. The limit is honoured (and capped at 100); the reader pages until totalCount is reached, at most 40 pages. Rows give title, full_location, apply_url, description, create_date, city, state and country.

**Public link** (`build_board.board_url`). board_url links the ref when it is a full address, else the company's website.

**robots.txt.** Not asked: read through ats.\_get as a feed. Not measured.

**Where it names its employer.** Stated on every posting: hiring_organization. verify_boards.board_says asks the first 50 postings and marks the names stated only when that page covers the count the site gives (or came back short of a full page); a longer site keeps its names unstated, for the owner's queue.

**Quirks.**

- Not what fetch_icims reads: a Jibe site answers ?in_iframe=1 with a 143-byte script that bounces back to the careers page and serves an Angular shell at the portal address, which is why BigBear.ai read as a JavaScript wall; its apply links still point back at the iCIMS portal.
- An empty read raises ('no jobs parsed from Jibe API'): Unknown, never a zero.

### Jobvite

`jobvite` · **read** · researched as build · reader `ats.fetch_jobvite` · identity probe `verify_boards._jobvite` · measured 2026-11-19, 2026-11-21, 2026-11-22

**How to spot it.** A link to a career site or one of its postings, jobs.jobvite.com/\<slug>[/...], never its \_\_assets\_\_: the first character cannot be an underscore (find_site_boards). The slug is the ref. Hint: jobvite.com.

**Forms the finder tallies apart** (`find_site_boards.ELSEWHERE`):

- `jobvite-joblink`: A link to ONE job, app.jobvite.com/j?cj=\<id>, whose account the link does not show; robots.txt closes its /j/ hop, so the slug cannot be learned from it (INRIX's).
- `jobvite-other`: Any other jobvite.com address, such as the embed loader jobs.jobvite.com/\_\_assets\_\_/scripts/careersite/public/iframe.js (NinjaOne's page serves only that, with no slug in its HTML).
- `jobvite-tenant`: An address naming a Jobvite account (a company code, c= or ci=, on app. or hire.jobvite.com: its CompanyJobs pages, its talent network and its widget) where this door does not read it as the account's own board: beside a jobs.jobvite.com career site their site names (another account beside their board, and a doubt), or on hire.jobvite.com. On app.jobvite.com, with no career site named anywhere on their site, the same address is a jobvitefeed board.

**How it publishes.** The career site's list page, server-rendered with every opening on it: GET https://jobs.jobvite.com/\<slug>/jobs, one row per opening (\<td class="jv-job-list-name"> with its /\<slug>/job/\<id> link, and its location cell), grouped under category headings. An embedded board's list and postings send a browser on to the employer's own careers page; asked with nl=1&fr=false they answer themselves. The ad and any stated pay are each posting's schema.org block, read from the posting itself (behind FETCH_DETAILS). No paging seen.

**Public link** (`build_board.board_url`). https://jobs.jobvite.com/\<slug>/jobs

**robots.txt.** Asked at every hop, and every hop held to jobs.jobvite.com/\<slug>/. Measured 2026-11-19..21: jobs.jobvite.com and search.jobvite.com have no robots.txt (404, so no rules); app.jobvite.com allows /CompanyJobs/Xml.aspx (the XML feed) and closes /j/, /Jobs/, /API/, /Careers/ and /Widget/.

**Where it names its employer.** The list page names its career site only in its \<title>, '\<Name> Careers', free text in a fixed pattern, so verify_boards.\_jobvite believes it only with what EVERY posting's schema.org hiringOrganization says (up to 40 postings asked): a posting naming nobody leaves the board unstated, and a board whose title and postings disagree states two names and goes to the owner's queue (Absolute's title says 'Absolute Security' and its postings 'Absolute Software', 2026-11-19).

**Quirks.**

- JOBVITE'S TENANTS SHARE ONE HOST AND DIFFER BY PATH: every read is held to jobs.jobvite.com/\<slug>/ before the hop is asked anything, a path that does not say plainly which career site it is ('..', escapes, backslashes) is refused, and a row is read only under the slug asked (blind reviews, 2026-11-22).
- A dead slug is sent to search.jobvite.com (?invalid=1): an error, never a zero. A list with no rows is an error too, until a real empty board has been read.
- The XML feed beside it (app.jobvite.com/CompanyJobs/Xml.aspx?c=\<company code>) is not read by this reader: it is the type jobvitefeed, read for an account whose site names no career site (Tyler's), by its company id.
- A posting's own block names its job by identifier (the job's id, measured 2026-11-22 on Gigamon's postings); only the node that is this posting gives a row its ad and its pay.
- A job open in several places shows only 'N Locations' on the list (Uplight's '2 Locations').
- discover_ats.MARKERS still files jobs.jobvite.com/\<slug> as type html.

**Notes.**

- The research said build, reading the HTML list nightly and the XML feed as paced enrichment for descriptions (and Tyler's pay); this reader was built on the list alone, and the feed got a reader of its own, jobvitefeed (2026-11-23), for an account with no career site to read. The code is what runs.
- The research proposed believing the title when ONE posting's JSON-LD agrees with it; the probe asks every posting, up to 40, after a blind review found one posting standing for a board (2026-11-22). The code is what runs.
- The research counted Gigamon's board at 21 on 2026-11-19; the reader's own note says 22, measured 2026-11-21.

### Jobvite (an account's XML feed)

`jobvitefeed` · **read** · researched as build · reader `ats.fetch_jobvitefeed` · identity probe `verify_boards._jobvitefeed` · measured 2026-11-20, 2026-11-23

**How to spot it.** An address on app.jobvite.com that names a Jobvite account by its company id, on a page of the company's own site that names no jobs.jobvite.com career site (find_site_boards): the widget's script, /\_\_assets\_\_/scripts/.../JV.getTPWidget.js?...ci=\<id>, its frame, /TalentNetwork/widget/widgetContainerV2.html?...ci=\<id>, a talent network link (/TalentNetwork/...?c=\<id>), or a CompanyJobs page (/CompanyJobs/Careers.aspx, Job.aspx or Xml.aspx ?...c=\<id>), each Tyler's shape on 2026-11-23. The id is the ref: 'q', four letters or digits, 'fw' and one more (q6NaVfwI). Where their site names a jobs.jobvite.com career site, that is the candidate and these addresses are jobvite-tenant, as before. Beside the account, only app.jobvite.com's addresses that name no board, on the widget's own page, are its furniture: a jobs.jobvite.com career site's loader or frame there (jobvite-other, naming no slug) stays a doubt (blind review 12, 2026-11-23). Hint: jobvite.com.

**How it publishes.** One GET of https://app.jobvite.com/CompanyJobs/Xml.aspx?c=\<id>: XML, every job of the account in one answer, with no paging and no total (Tyler's on 2026-11-23: 2,119,266 characters, 266 rows). A \<result> of \<job>s, each with id, title, requisitionid, category, jobtype, location ('City, ST, Country'), date (M/D/YYYY), detail-url and apply-url (CDATA, http), description (the whole ad, as escaped HTML), briefdescription, and the fields the account adds (Tyler's: company_x0020_name, hiring_x0020_manager, agency_x0020_access, and salarymin, salarymax, salarycurrency and salaryfrequency on 213 rows). A job open in several places is a parent row and one row per other place (parentId, 139 of Tyler's 266), so one row per job is read, the copies' places joined to the parent's: 127 jobs. The ad is in the same answer.

**Public link** (`build_board.board_url`). https://app.jobvite.com/CompanyJobs/Careers.aspx?c=\<id>, Jobvite's own careers page for the account (robots.txt allows it; nobody here has opened it yet), never the feed. Each row links its own job page, the feed's detail-url as https.

**robots.txt.** Asked, and no redirect followed: the feed answers in place, so a hop anywhere, back to the feed's own address included, is refused before it is asked (blind review 12, 2026-11-23). Measured 2026-11-19..21 and 2026-11-23: app.jobvite.com allows /CompanyJobs/ (the feed, Job.aspx, Careers.aspx) and closes /j/, /Jobs/, /API/, /Careers/ and /Widget/. It answered 429 (Retry-After 30) to a second feed asked a second after the first, so its gate holds requests 30 seconds apart (ats.JOBVITE_FEED_PAUSE), and nothing it answers is cached (ats.NEVER_CACHED).

**Where it names its employer.** Only in the feed's own fields, and the feed is the whole board in one answer, so verify_boards.\_jobvitefeed believes a name the feed states on EVERY row: \<company> where any row fills it (and then it must be the same on every row), else the custom company-name field, company_x0020_name, present and the same on every row. A field empty or missing on one row states nothing; rows that disagree, or a company-name field naming another name beside \<company>, are two names stated, which proven() refuses. Measured: Tyler's feed has no \<company> and 'Tyler Technologies' in company_x0020_name on 266 of 266 rows; Absolute's \<company> is 'Absolute Security' on 18 of 18; Gigamon's \<company> is empty on 26 of 26, so it states nothing (2026-11-20).

**Quirks.**

- A PERSON'S NAME ON EVERY ROW: hiring_x0020_manager names one on all of Tyler's 266 rows (and Absolute's 18 and Gigamon's 26). The reader keeps the fields it uses by name (ats.\_JVX_FIELDS) and drops every other field's text as it parses, so no person's name reaches a row, a note, stderr, the probe's answer or a cache.
- Parsed as XML by expat: a DOCTYPE or an ENTITY declaration is refused before anything it declares is read; a feed cut short, one that is not a \<result> of \<job>s, one listing no job and one over 32,000,000 bytes are errors, never a zero or part of a board; more than 2 rows that do not read as a job of the account (no id, no title, a job page of another account) are an error too.
- One row per job: a parent and its per-location copies (parentId), grouped whatever their order. The parent gives the row its title, date, job page, category, pay and ad; each copy adds its place, once.
- A company id nobody holds is sent 302 to app.jobvite.com/Recruiting/Home.aspx and on to Jobvite's own site (research, 2026-11-20): every hop off the feed's address is refused before it is asked, so it is an error, never a zero.
- posted is the row's \<date>, M/D/YYYY. The research found it is not always the posting's own datePosted (Absolute's oFV3AfwX: 11/4/2026 in its feed, 2026-11-02 on its posting, and 11 of its 18 rows share 10/19/2026).
- Pay only from the row's own salary fields: the ISO code out of 'US Dollar (USD US$)', a period only from Annually, Annual, Yearly, Monthly, Weekly, Daily or Hourly (Bi-Weekly is not a week), cents kept (20.00-22.50 is not 20-22), and a figure that does not read publishes no pay.
- The ad goes into jd only behind FETCH_DETAILS, though it costs no request more (asked so, 2026-11-23).

**Notes.**

- Not the type jobvite: a slug names a career site and a company id an account, and nothing on a page ties one to the other. A board on file as one is not known to be the same board as one found as the other.
- The research of 2026-11-20 proposed reading the career site's HTML nightly and the feed only as paced enrichment, never storing its hiring-manager field; the feed is read as a board of its own where the account's site names no career site. The code is what runs.
- hire.jobvite.com's CompanyJobs pages name an account by c= too; no site measured here uses one, so the finder leaves them a jobvite-tenant doubt.

### Lever

`lever` · **read** · reader `ats.fetch_lever` · identity probe `verify_boards.board_says` · measured 2026-08-23, 2026-11-18

**How to spot it.** jobs.lever.co/\<slug> (find_boards.PATTERNS and discover_ats.MARKERS, borrowed by find_site_boards) and the API address api.lever.co/v0/postings/\<slug>, which a page that draws its own list calls (the finder's own; Softdocs, 2026-11-18). Hint: lever.co. The slug is kept as the page spelt it: Lever minds case.

**Forms the finder tallies apart** (`find_site_boards.ELSEWHERE`):

- `lever-eu`: A board in Lever's European region (jobs.eu.lever.co/\<x>); fetch_lever asks the American API only, so it is tallied apart.

**How it publishes.** A documented JSON API, one GET: https://api.lever.co/v0/postings/\<slug>?mode=json -> a bare list of postings with text, categories.location, hostedUrl, createdAt (epoch milliseconds), workplaceType, country (ISO-2, no city or region), the ad across five fields (descriptionPlain, openingPlain, lists, additionalPlain, salaryDescriptionPlain) and salaryRange. No paging.

**Public link** (`build_board.board_url`). https://jobs.lever.co/\<slug>

**robots.txt.** Not asked for the feed (ats.\_get, exempt under the owner's ruling of 2026-10-09). The identity probe reads the board's page, jobs.lever.co/\<slug>, through verify_boards.\_board_page, robots.txt at every hop, as a stream cut after 64 KB. Not measured.

**Where it names its employer.** The feed names nobody. The board's own page states the display name the employer set in Lever, in its twitter:title meta (not \<title>, which carries whatever trailing space the employer typed, nor og:title, which adds 'jobs'): verify_boards.board_says reads the feed, then \_lever_page. 'Swiftly, Inc.' where the slug is goswift.

**Quirks.**

- Lever minds case: asked 2026-11-18, api.lever.co answered nine postings for 'Wayground' and HTTP 404 for 'wayground', and two of the 33 Lever boards then on file were spelt with a capital. Compare Lever refs without regard to case when asking whether a board is already held.
- No one field is the ad: descriptionPlain is the opening paragraph only, so the reader joins all five, deduplicated by containment.
- The board page is some 700 KB of inlined CSS with the name in its first kilobyte (jobs.lever.co/goswift: 714,503 bytes, 2026-11-18), so the probe reads its first 64 KB.
- Lever sends a country and no city or region, so office_hint can place a role in a country, never in a state.

### Oracle Recruiting Cloud

`oracle` · **read** · reader `ats.fetch_oracle` · no identity probe · measured unknown

**How to spot it.** \<x>.fa.\<y>.oraclecloud.com. Discovery (discover_ats.MARKERS) files the host as type oracle, the host being the ref. find_site_boards does not take it as a board: fetch_oracle reads site CX_1 only, so a tenant with a named site cannot be read, and the finder tallies the host under elsewhere as 'oraclecloud' until it can.

**Forms the finder tallies apart** (`find_site_boards.ELSEWHERE`):

- `oraclecloud`: An Oracle Recruiting Cloud host (\<x>.fa.\<y>.oraclecloud.com). It is in neither TENANT_FORMS nor \_NO_BOARD_IN_IT, so the finder's summary counts it under 'no reader for', although fetch_oracle exists.

**How it publishes.** JSON: \<host>/hcmRestApi/resources/latest/recruitingCEJobRequisitions?onlyData=true&finder=findReqs;siteNumber=CX_1 -> items[].requisitionList[] with Title, PrimaryLocation, Id and ShortDescription or ExternalDescriptionStr. One reply, never paged.

**Public link** (`build_board.board_url`). board_url links the ref when it is a full address, else the company's website.

**robots.txt.** Not asked: read through ats.\_get. Not measured.

**Where it names its employer.** No identity probe: verify_boards.board_says answers 'no identity probe written for oracle'.

**Quirks.**

- UNVERIFIED: no company on file used the type when the reader was written, so nothing live was probed, and an empty Oracle description is not 'this tenant publishes no descriptions'.
- Its size cannot be asked (the reader takes one reply and never pages: wire_found.PARTIAL), so the wiring door skips every Oracle find; whether Oracle finds are worth a way to ask is the owner's to settle.

`paylocity` · **read** · reader `ats.fetch_paylocity` · identity probe `verify_boards._paylocity` · measured 2026-08-23, 2026-11-18, 2026-11-22

Description is a \~110-character preview cut mid-word, flagged \_jd_is_teaser so no money pattern runs over it; the posting page carries no more. One request; no paging.

**Public link** (`build_board.board_url`). The ref (a full address).

**robots.txt.** Asked at every hop (ats.\_page). Not measured.

**Where it names its employer.** Stated on the board's own page: pageData.ModuleTitle, the name the employer gave the board, never the address's tail (Centegix's ends '34ED-LLC', Circuit's 'TFR-Transit-Inc'). verify_boards.\_paylocity also gives the board's own /jobs/All/\<uuid> address from og:url, when the page's LeadJoinUrl, if any, names the same uuid: an address, never a name.

- One board, two ids: FAAC's frame is /List/2115/FAAC-Incorporated and lands on /All/\<uuid>/FAAC-Incorporated (2026-11-18). The finder folds the two when one page names both, and wire_found asks a board found by /List/ for the /All/ address its page states (2026-11-22).
- The tenant's name after the id is not always there (Celona's record reads .../All/\<uuid> bare), so the wiring door holds a board whose two addresses cannot be compared.

### Pinpoint

`pinpoint` · **read** · researched as build · reader `ats.fetch_pinpoint` · identity probe `verify_boards._pinpoint` · measured 2026-11-19, 2026-11-21

**How to spot it.** \<slug>.pinpointhq.com in an href, a script, an iframe or a browser's request (find_site_boards; www, app and api are the vendor's own hosts). The slug is the ref, lowered; it is not the company id ('clearview' for clearview-ai). Hint: pinpointhq.com.

**Forms the finder tallies apart** (`find_site_boards.ELSEWHERE`):

- `pinpoint-other`: An address on pinpointhq.com that names no tenant.

**How it publishes.** Two board-level requests and none per posting: GET https://\<slug>.pinpointhq.com/postings.json -> {data: [...]}, the feed Pinpoint's own careers widget calls (title, url, location.name, workplace_type, the ad in four HTML fields each under the employer's own heading, compensation_minimum, compensation_maximum, compensation_currency and compensation_frequency with compensation_visible), and /jobs.rss, which the board itself links as rel=alternate, for the posted date (each item's pubDate, joined by job.id). No paging: ?page=2 is ignored.

**Public link** (`build_board.board_url`). https://\<slug>.pinpointhq.com

**robots.txt.** Asked at every hop (read as pages, held to the host), because robots.txt is per tenant. Measured 2026-11-19..21: the standard tenant file disallows only /mydata, /admin and /companies; infor.pinpointhq.com is Disallow: / (and discovery recorded coursedog.pinpointhq.com refused the same way on 2026-11-15); eptura.pinpointhq.com also disallows two postings, in the canonical /postings/\<uuid> form.

**Where it names its employer.** Not in the feed. The board states 'Careers at X' in two places of its own, its RSS channel title and its front page's og:title, and verify_boards.\_pinpoint believes X only when the two agree. An empty board still states it (Democracy Works). Never the slug.

**Quirks.**

- Pay is read only when compensation_visible is true; every comp field was null on the rows with it false.
- location.name is the employer's own words ('Hybrid - Washington, DC', 'Remote USA'); city and province are unreliable (London's province reads 'United Kingdom') and there is no country, so only the city goes into office_hint.
- reporting_to names a hiring manager on some rows and is never read; the RSS body repeats it as 'Reporting To', so the ad comes from the JSON fields.
- A dates feed that will not read costs the dates, never the board.
- The widget form \<div data-pinpoint-subdomain="\<slug>"> (Democracy Works' careers page) carries no pinpointhq.com host, so the finder's markup patterns miss it; the host appears only in a rendered page's request to the feed.
- discover_ats.MARKERS still files \<label>.pinpointhq.com as type html.

**Notes.**

- The research advised testing each posting's canonical /postings/\<uuid> path against the tenant's cached robots rules and dropping a refused row (Eptura disallows postings in that form while the feed hands out /en/postings/\<uuid>); fetch_pinpoint does not. Neither refused posting was in the feed when measured. The code is what runs.

### SAP SuccessFactors (Career Site Builder)

`successfactors` · **read** · researched as maybe · reader `ats.fetch_successfactors` · identity probe `verify_boards._successfactors` · measured 2026-11-19..2026-11-23

**Why maybe.** Read since 2026-11-22 (ats.fetch_successfactors), built when the owner asked for Gainwell Technologies' board: classic Career Site Builder boards from their server-drawn /search/ list. Unify boards, whose list is served only by POST /services/recruiting/v1/jobs (robots-closed), are read since 2026-11-23 from their sitemap.xml and each posting's own page, two requests a posting (ats.successfactors_unify; the owner's word for Aurigo, Esri Canada and Octave, who accepted the cost). The research (2026-11-20) rated the platform maybe: Classic Career Site Builder boards are a clean public listing: server-rendered /search/ pages on the employer's own careers host, 25 rows a page, robots-allowed, no token. Three things hold it at maybe. The newer 'Unify' search draws its results by POST /services/recruiting/v1/jobs, which every CSB robots.txt closes, leaving only sitemap.xml plus one or two requests per posting. The legacy portals companies link (careerN.successfactors.com, careerN.sapsf.com ?company=) are closed outright. And under the owner's rule only 2 of the 8 example companies would wire unattended (Landis+Gyr, and Indra Group, a 623-posting Spanish board): the rest are a parent's board, a placeholder name or a longer registered name. Worth building as a classic-CSB reader that detects Unify and reports Unknown, or falls back to the sitemap if the owner accepts the cost per posting.

**How to spot it.** A page of the company's own site that IS a classic CSB board, by its tells - assets under rmkcdn.successfactors.com/\<8 hex>/, a j2w.init({... ssoCompanyId ...}) block, jQuery from an hcm\<N> or performancemanager\<N> (sapsf|successfactors) host, or /platform/js/j2w/ scripts - read only from the page's own scripts and attributes: the board's ref is that page's scheme and host. A link to https://\<host>/go/\<Name>/\<digits>/ or /search/?...sortColumn=... on the company's own registrable domain gives that origin too. Never a ref from an SAP host. Legacy portals (career\<N>.successfactors.(com|eu), career\<N>.sapsf.(com|eu|cn), ?company=) are the vendor form successfactors-legacy: robots-closed, never a board.

**Forms the finder tallies apart** (`find_site_boards.ELSEWHERE`):

- `successfactors-legacy`: A legacy Recruiting Management portal address, career\<N>.successfactors.(com|eu) or career\<N>.sapsf.(com|eu|cn) at /career or /careers?company=\<id>: robots.txt closes it ('Disallow: /'), so it is a platform the crawl cannot read and a doubt beside a board - except on a CSB board's own pages, where it is furniture (the j2w.init ssoUrl, a sign-in link).
- `successfactors-other`: Another SAP SuccessFactors address that names no board (assets, an hcm\<N> host, an API host).

**How it publishes.** Classic: GET https://\<board host>/search/?q=&sortColumn=referencedate&sortDirection=desc&startrow=\<0, 25, 50, ...>, server-rendered HTML (\<table id="searchresults">, one \<tr class="data-row"> a posting: the jobTitle-link, jobLocation, jobDate and per-site columns), offset-paged 25 at a time with the total in the localized pagination label; category pages /go/\<Name>/\<catid>/\<startrow>/ carry the same table. Description and pay are only on each /job/\<slug>/\<id>/ page. Unify: the /search/ page lists nothing (POST /services/recruiting/v1/jobs draws the list in the browser); the robots-clean list is https://\<board host>/sitemap.xml, a \<urlset> of one \<loc> a posting at /job/\<slug>/\<id>/, XML-escaped, every \<lastmod> one day (not a posted date). Each loc answers 302 to /job/\<slug>/\<N>-\<locale>/, and one role's English and French copies land on the same N. The posting page shows the role in itemprop="title", the ad in itemprop="description" and the tenant's own labelled tokens (a place - Posting Location, Job Location (Short) - or Country; Workplace Type; Posting Start Date, M/D/YY on en-US). Measured 2026-11-23: Aurigo 16 locs, Esri Canada 32 (16 roles, each in English and French), Octave 131. RSS exists under /services/rss/ and is closed. Measured on Gainwell 2026-11-22: jobs.gainwelltechnologies.com, 334 postings over 14 pages of 25, read in full in 15 requests; remote roles carry a placeholder place ('Any city, TX, US, 99999'), which the reader reads as 'TX, US'.

**robots.txt.** Measured 2026-11-19..21: a byte-identical CSB template robots.txt on all six board hosts read allows /search/, /go/, /job/ and /sitemap.xml, and disallows /services/ (the RSS and the Unify API), /talentcommunity/apply/, /applybutton/ and /preapply/. The legacy portals (career8.successfactors.com, career41.sapsf.com) serve 'Disallow: /', 'Disallow: /\*company', 'Allow: /login' and were never asked.

**Where it names its employer.** Stated on the board's own host: the /search/ page's \<title>, '{site name} Jobs', and its meta description, 'Find at {site name}' (localized: 'JENOPTIK AG - Stellen', 'Buscar en Indra Group'); classic posting pages add \<meta itemprop="hiringOrganization">. The site name is whatever the admin typed: a placeholder on 2 of 6 boards ('esricanada', 'our team'), and a group's board names the parent. The ssoCompanyId in j2w.init is a tenant id, not a name. A Unify posting page names no hiringOrganization: its \<title> is '\<role> Job Details | \<site name>' (translated on a French page), and the probe reads the site name after its last ' | ' ('Aurigo Software Technologies', 'esricanada', 'Octave', measured 2026-11-23).

**Quirks.**

- Group boards name the parent and carry many units: SPX's 237 rows covered 12 units, the unit only in a site-specific 'Facility' column spelt inconsistently, where Landis+Gyr's same column holds requisition ids.
- Templates are localized (en_US, de_DE and es_ES seen): the \<title>, the meta description, the pagination label and the date format follow the site's default locale; pass locale=en_US where a site offers English.
- Multilingual tenants list one role once per language under different ids.
- A /go/ category page can carry an empty \<title>: read the name from /search/.
- Giants among the examples: Indra Group 623 postings (mostly Spain), SPX 237, Jenoptik 175.
- Unify sitemaps escape their locs (&apos;, &amp;), and Esri Canada's server writes a French posting's redirect Location encoded twice; the reader keeps the sitemap's own address as the row's.

**Notes.**

- Gainwell Technologies' board states 'Gainwell Technologies LLC' (the /search/ title and description, and the hiringOrganization of its postings), proven for the record.
- Unify boards (Aurigo, Esri Canada, Octave) are read from their sitemap since 2026-11-23, so far only offline over the responses saved that day: Aurigo 16 rows, Esri Canada 16 (32 locs, each role's two languages paired by requisition), Octave 131; none is wired yet. The probe states 'Aurigo Software Technologies' whole, which proves Aurigo's record only through its also_known_as 'Aurigo Software Technologies Inc.', and 'esricanada' whole, which proves no record (the country on 'Esri Canada' is not on the board's name); Octave's 131 are not stated whole.
- A Unify posting's ad is read from its first itemprop="description" element only, as the classic reader's is; Esri Canada's postings split theirs into three, the pay sentence in the third, and their Salary Min/Max tokens are not read.

### Teamtailor

`teamtailor` · **read** · researched as build · reader `ats.fetch_teamtailor` · identity probe `verify_boards._teamtailor` · measured 2026-11-19, 2026-11-21, 2026-11-22

**How to spot it.** \<label>.teamtailor.com or \<label>.na.teamtailor.com (its North American data centre; the region label is part of the site's address) in a link, script or frame, the vendor's own labels skipped (find_site_boards). A career site on a domain of the company's own names no teamtailor.com host: the finder spots it when one page both loads assets from teamtailor-cdn.com and links its own \<host>/jobs.rss as rel=alternate (teamtailor_own_sites). The ref is the site's origin. Hint: teamtailor.

**Forms the finder tallies apart** (`find_site_boards.ELSEWHERE`):

- `teamtailor-other`: An address on teamtailor.com or teamtailor-cdn.com that names no career site: the 'Powered by Teamtailor' link (tt.teamtailor.com), assets, and the widget embed (scripts.teamtailor-cdn.com/widgets/\<region>/jobs.js with a div carrying data-teamtailor-api-key), which gives no board host.

**How it publishes.** A JSON Feed of the whole board, which the site announces for programs (its /.well-known/api-catalog lists it): GET https://\<host>/jobs.json -> {version: 'https://jsonfeed.org/version/1.1', title, feed_url, items[]}, each item with title, url, date_published, content_html (the whole ad) and a \_jobposting block (jobLocation[], hiringOrganization, and baseSalary when the employer fills Teamtailor's salary field). One request; no paging offered or needed.

**Public link** (`build_board.board_url`). The ref (the site's origin).

**robots.txt.** Asked at every hop (read as a page, held to its host). Measured 2026-11-19..21: the same Teamtailor robots.txt on all seven hosts read (two EU, one North American, four on companies' own domains) allows /jobs.json, /jobs.rss, /jobs and the postings, and disallows only /app/, /messages/, /messenger/, /facebook/tab/ and /jobs/internal/.

**Where it names its employer.** Stated by the feed: its own title and every posting's \_jobposting.hiringOrganization.name, and verify_boards.\_teamtailor states all of them, so a site posting for two companies shows both. A site with nothing open still has its title (Heimdall Power, Corporater, Gecko, Heja). It never states a website: hiringOrganization.sameAs is the career site itself.

**Quirks.**

- ON A DOMAIN OF THEIR OWN THE HOST CANNOT VOUCH FOR THE VENDOR, so the body must: a JSON Feed whose feed_url is on the host asked and whose every item carries \_jobposting.
- An empty feed on a company's own domain is a zero only when the answer's Content-Security-Policy names app(.na).teamtailor.com as the page allowed to frame the site; otherwise 'the zero is not known'. The header is kept with a cached body (ats.KEPT_HEADERS), because a 304 replay without it read Heimdall Power's empty board as not known (2026-11-22).
- addressRegion was null on every US posting read, so a US row gets a city and a country and no state.
- The older discovery patterns read fonrochelightingamerica.na.teamtailor.com as the slug 'na' (discover_js) or the host na.teamtailor.com (discover_ats); find_site_boards keeps the region, and discover_ats.MARKERS still files \<label>.teamtailor.com as type html.
- Feeds carry evergreen talent-pool posts that are not openings (Copenhagen Optimization's 'Talent Pool - Consultancy CPH').
- Widget-only embeds (greehill's) are not read: reaching them would mean lifting a key from someone's page.

**Notes.**

- The research said an empty feed should read as none open; the code reads it so only on a teamtailor.com host, or on a company's own domain whose answer names Teamtailor in its Content-Security-Policy, because an empty JSON Feed vouches for nothing. The code is what runs.

### Workable

`workable` · **read** · reader `ats.fetch_workable` · identity probe `verify_boards.board_says` · measured 2026-08-23, 2026-11-01, 2026-11-19

**How to spot it.** apply.workable.com/\<slug> (find_boards.PATTERNS and discover_ats.MARKERS, borrowed by find_site_boards), a \<slug>@jobs.workablemail.com forwarding mailbox (Nallian's careers page carried no other tell), and the finder's own forms: the API addresses apply.workable.com/api/v1 or v3/[widget/]accounts/\<slug or number> and the older \<account>.workable.com host. Hint: workable.

**How it publishes.** A documented JSON API, the careers widget's, one GET: https://apply.workable.com/api/v1/widget/accounts/\<slug>?details=true -> {name, jobs: [...]} with title, city, state, country, url, published_on, telecommuting and, with details=true, the description. Workable publishes no pay field of its own. No paging.

**Public link** (`build_board.board_url`). https://apply.workable.com/\<slug>; a numbered account links the company's website instead, because apply.workable.com/\<number> is Workable's error page.

**robots.txt.** Not asked (ats.\_get, exempt under the owner's ruling of 2026-10-09). Not measured.

**Where it names its employer.** Stated in the feed: the account's name (name, or account.name), read by verify_boards.board_says from the same widget request; judge() reads it with the older substring test.

**Quirks.**

- One job is listed once for each country it is open in, with the same address, so only the rows that would collide take city, state and country as the location (IRTH's two Cloud Engineer rows broke the nightly self-test, 2026-11-01).
- A page embedding Workable's widget asks for the board by the account's NUMBER (.../widget/accounts/\<number>), which reads and does not open: the wiring door follows one posting to its landing address for the slug, holds the slug to the number, and wires the slug or nothing (2026-11-19).
- telecommuting true means remote; false asserts nothing.

### Workday

`workday` · **read** · reader `ats.fetch_workday` · no identity probe · measured 2026-08-23, 2026-09-01, 2026-11-16, 2026-11-18

**How to spot it.** \<tenant>.\<wdN>.myworkdayjobs.com/[\<locale>/]\<site>, and the API address a rendered page calls, \<tenant>.\<wdN>.myworkdayjobs.com/wday/cxs/\<tenant>/\<site>/jobs, where the site is the fourth path segment and 'wday' is not a site (find_site_boards' own patterns; discovery's marker skips only en-US and is not borrowed). The ref is the list [tenant, pod, site]: the pod ('wd5', 'wd12') is never guessable and comes out of the address found. Hint: myworkdayjobs.com.

**Forms the finder tallies apart** (`find_site_boards.ELSEWHERE`):

- `workday-myworkdaysite`: Workday's other host, wdN.myworkdaysite.com/recruiting/\<tenant>/\<site>, which is pod-first; the finder tallies it apart because, in its own words, ats.fetch_workday cannot take its pod-first refs today.
- `workday-no-site`: wdN.myworkdayjobs.com with no tenant or site named; a redirect that lands on one is walked one hop further, since Workday's next hop is usually the board.

**How it publishes.** JSON by POST: https://\<tenant>.\<pod>.myworkdayjobs.com/wday/cxs/\<tenant>/\<site>/jobs with {limit: 20, offset, searchText}. The reader asks two searches only, 'account executive' and 'sales', and pages each by offset, 20 at a time (50 and 100 answer HTTP 400), at most 60 pages a search. The search gives title, locationsText and externalPath; the ad is at /wday/cxs/\<tenant>/\<site>\<externalPath> (behind FETCH_DETAILS). ats.workday_total asks the whole board's size: total on the first reply to an empty search.

**Public link** (`build_board.board_url`). None of its own: the ref is a list, so board_url links the company's website.

**robots.txt.** Not asked: JSON requests by POST (ats.\_post_json). Not measured.

**Where it names its employer.** No identity probe: verify_boards.board_says answers 'no identity probe written for workday', so no Workday board can pass proven().

**Quirks.**

- Past the end of a search Workday WRAPS to page one (verified 2026-09-01 on motorolasolutions: offsets 180, 200 and 300 each returned offset 0's rows), so ats.\_paged stops on a page that adds nothing new; total is true only on the first reply of a walk (161 at offset 0, 0 at offsets 20 to 160).
- The reader filters, so its rows say nothing about a board's size: Motorola Solutions' board held 868 postings by its own count on a day the reader returned 385 rows (2026-11-18). The wiring door asks workday_total first and skips a giant unread (wire_found.PARTIAL).
- One gate for every tenant: Workday's limit is on the caller, not the tenant, so all its hosts share one host gate and one backoff (2026-11-16: 39 of 42 tenants answered 429 to GitHub's runners in both crawls of the day).
- Read from the owner's Mac (his ruling of 2026-11-17): scripts/workday_snapshot.py runs there and commits data/workday_snapshot.json, and the nightly crawl (GOVTECH_DOCK_WORKDAY_SNAPSHOT=1) takes a board from it; a board the Mac has not read in 48 hours is asked live, and a failure names the snapshot's age.

**Notes.**

- Code against code: fetch_workday's docstring says it reads both hosts, but its myworkdaysite branch is taken only when the ref's first two parts both start with 'wd', which its own example ('wd3', 'modaxo', 'Tadera') does not; called with the network stubbed on 2026-11-22, that ref was asked at wd3.modaxo.myworkdayjobs.com. find_site_boards says fetch_workday cannot take pod-first refs today and tallies the host apart (workday-myworkdaysite).

### Zoho Recruit

`zohorecruit` · **read** · researched as build · reader `ats.fetch_zohorecruit` · identity probe `verify_boards._zohorecruit` · measured 2026-11-19, 2026-11-21

**How to spot it.** A link to a career site or one of its postings, https://\<portal>.zohorecruit.\<com|eu|in>/jobs/\<PageName>[/...], or the embed rec_embed_js.load({site: 'https://\<portal>.zohorecruit.com', page_name: 'Careers', ...}), whose bare site is not a board without its page's name (find_site_boards). The ref is the page's address on Zoho's own host, even for a tenant on a custom domain. Hint: zohorecruit.

**Forms the finder tallies apart** (`find_site_boards.ELSEWHERE`):

- `zohorecruit-other`: Zoho Recruit's own hosts (www, static, cdn, help, blog, api, accounts).
- `zohorecruit-tenant`: A tenant's host with no page named: a portal whose board this door cannot name, maybe a parent's, filed apart as a doubt unless it is the very tenant a board on the page already is.

**How it publishes.** A server-rendered page of some 1.8 MB carrying the whole list as JSON in a hidden \<input id="jobs"> and the board's facts in another (id="meta": list_url and org_info), both at the very end, after an inlined asset map, so the page is read whole. One request; no paging seen (the largest board read held 31 rows).

**Public link** (`build_board.board_url`). The ref (the career site's address).

**robots.txt.** Asked at every hop (read as a page, held to its host). Measured 2026-11-19..21: an identical Zoho robots.txt on every tenant read allows /jobs, /jobs/ and /jobs/\* and disallows everything else; the embed widget's lighter JSON (/recruit/v2/public/Job_Openings) is closed, and a live read of it was refused.

**Where it names its employer.** Stated on the page the reader reads: the meta input's org_info.company_name, with org_info.website, which proven() holds to the one on file. It is the ACCOUNT's name, so a parent's board states the parent (QuickLaunch's link goes to ElevenX Capital's). verify_boards.\_zohorecruit states nothing for a board set to hide its name, nor for any page but the account's default 'Careers'. Never the page title ('Jobs at Careers' on Cuseum's) nor the portal label ('exc' is ElevenX).

**Quirks.**

- CLOSED JOBS ARE IN THE LIST: a row with Publish false is a job kept on view and closed (GovEase's only row, a 2025 opening), so only Publish true is read.
- Every wrong address answers 200 with a page saying so, so a page without the jobs input is an error, never a zero; the input's literal [] is a zero.
- On some layouts the description is a 153-character teaser ending '...' (Spektra's, ElevenX's): flagged \_jd_is_teaser and never read for money.
- The row has no address: the list's own address plus the id answers with the job, whatever its title becomes.
- A custom domain serves the same board (careers.spektrasystems.com); the vendor's host is the one a probe can hold every read to.

**Notes.**

- The research proposed the probe state org_info.company_name whenever hide_company_name is not true; the code also states nothing for any page but 'Careers', since the name is the account's and a sister brand's page would be proven for it (blind review, 2026-11-21). The code is what runs.

## Researched: worth a reader, not built yet

### Trakstar Hire (formerly Recruiterbox)

`trakstar` · **build** · no reader · no identity probe · measured 2026-11-19..2026-11-21

**Why build.** Every tenant serves a public RSS 2.0 feed of the whole board that its own page links ('Jobs RSS Feed') and robots.txt allows: one request a company, with title, link, the full ad, pubDate and city, state and country as fields. The feed names the employer by the display name it set, which equalled the name on file on all four boards read, and a made-up slug answers a clean 404 on its own host, so a dead board cannot pass as an empty one. The payoff today is small: 4 companies, 11 postings, none of them a sales title.

**How to spot it.** Tenants live at \<slug>.hire.trakstar.com; legacy \<slug>.recruiterbox.com links 301 there. Nothing in the finder names either host, in BOARDS or in ELSEWHERE (a job frame from one is tallied as other:trakstar.com). trakstar.com, not recruiterbox.com, is on the vendor-host lists (build_board.\_PROMOTE_ATS_HOSTS, refresh.\_ATS_HOSTS, admin.ATS_HOSTS). Every form the research saw was a plain link: the board home, a posting with ?apply=true, a posting with ?source=. Reduce a posting link to its tenant and read the board, never the posting.

**How it publishes.** RSS 2.0 with xmlns:job: GET https://\<slug>.hire.trakstar.com/jobfeeds/\<slug>, unpaged as far as measured (8 of 8 and 3 of 3 openings in one response): each item's title, link, description (the full ad as escaped HTML), pubDate, job:locationCity, job:locationState, job:locationCountry, job:positionType, job:team and job:closeDte. The board page, https://\<slug>.hire.trakstar.com/, is server-rendered and gives the count (RB.init_data.total_jobs), the identity statement and the work mode in one more request.

**robots.txt.** Measured 2026-11-19..21 on four tenants (identical files): User-agent: \* / Disallow: /prepare\* / Disallow: /published_jobs_list_v2\* / Allow: /. The board page, the RSS feed, the postings and the sitemap are allowed; /published_jobs_list_v2, the board's own list endpoint, is closed and must never be used. The legacy recruiterbox.com host serves the same file and 301s to the tenant.

**Where it names its employer.** Stated in the feed: \<channel>\<title>Jobs at {Name}\</title> and \<description>Current open positions at {Name}\</description>; also the board page's \<title> and h1, and each posting's JSON-LD hiringOrganization. A pattern statement, like Gusto's 'Careers at X': a probe should take X from 'Jobs at X' and require it to equal the X in 'Current open positions at X'. An empty board's feed still states its name (Selerix). No probe is written.

**Quirks.**

- Two dates that disagree: pubDate is RFC 822 at midnight +0530 (converting it to UTC moves it back a day), and a posting's JSON-LD datePosted differed from it on 4 of 9 postings compared, in both directions. Leave posted None, or take pubDate's calendar date with the owner's say-so.
- Pay is free text only, with no currency stated, and 7 of RideCo's 8 roles are in Ontario, where '$' means CAD.
- The feed's links are http:// with the stored client-name casing (RideCo.hire...); normalise them to https://\<slug, lowered>.hire.trakstar.com/jobs/\<id>/ so posting ids stay stable. The feed path ignores case, so store the slug lowered.
- Posting pages' JSON-LD holds raw control characters, so ats.\_schema_posting (a strict json.loads) gets nothing from them.
- Careers pages carry stale posting links (Focus School Software's linked posting is a 404 while its board is live).

## Researched: cannot or should not be read

### Paycom

`paycom` · **skip** · no reader · no identity probe · measured 2026-11-19..2026-11-21

**Why skip.** robots.txt leaves no way to read a Paycom job list. Both Paycom hosts serve Disallow: /, with Allow lines only for the career portal pages, single postings and two per-posting APIs. The old server-rendered list (jobs?clientkey=) is closed; the new career page is a JavaScript shell with no rows; its rows come from a POST to a closed host that needs a token minted into each page view; the sitemap answers 404. A reader would have to scrape a token and post to a disallowed path, which the owner's rules rule out.

**How to spot it.** Any paycomonline.net or paycomonline.com address: find_site_boards tallies it as 'paycom'. Seen as an href or iframe to www.paycomonline.net/v4/ats/web.php/jobs?clientkey=\<KEY> (sometimes with &fromClientSide=true), as per-posting jobs/ViewJobDetails?clientkey=\<KEY>&job=\<N> links, and as portal /v4/ats/web.php/portal/\<KEY>/jobs/\<N> links. The client key is 32 upper-case hex characters and names nobody. discover_ats.MARKERS files the old jobs?clientkey= form as type html, an address robots.txt closes, and misses the other two.

**How it publishes.** Old list: GET www.paycomonline.net/v4/ats/web.php/jobs?clientkey=\<KEY> (closed). New career page: /v4/ats/web.php/portal/\<KEY>/career-page, allowed, a \~235 KB shell with no rows. The rows: POST https://portal-applicant-tracking.us-cent.paycomonline.net/api/ats/job-posting-previews/search with the page's sessionJWT as its Authorization (closed, and token-gated). Open: one posting page at a time, /v4/ats/web.php/portal/\<KEY>/jobs/\<N>, with a schema.org JobPosting; its ids have to come from somewhere else.

**robots.txt.** Measured 2026-11-19..21: both Paycom hosts serve Disallow: /, with Allow only for /v4/ats/web.php/portal/, assets, /api/ats/job-postings/, /api/ats/company-name and /api/ats/portal-settings. The old list and ViewJobDetails were refused before any request; the job-posting-previews search is refused; the allowed APIs answered 401 without the page's token; /v4/ats/sitemap.php is allowed and answered 404.

**Where it names its employer.** Never at the board's level: the career page is titled 'Job Opportunities'. Each posting page names its employer in its JobPosting hiringOrganization.name, a payroll-style legal name in capitals ('VIMO INC', 'CODE FOUR'), one posting at a time. No probe.

**Quirks.**

- A smaller job than a reader: where an employer links its postings one by one (Code Four's page does), each old ViewJobDetails?clientkey=K&job=N link can be rewritten to the allowed /v4/ats/web.php/portal/K/jobs/N, which ats.\_schema_posting reads unchanged. The owner should rule on that rewrite before it is built.
- A posting page alone does not prove a job is open: Code Four's 2021 posting still answered 200, with no validThrough.
- The discovery log marks companies retry_soon after a robots refusal of the old Paycom address; that refusal is not transient, so the retries keep failing.
