### Paycor Recruiting

`paycor` · **skip** · no reader · no identity probe · measured 2026-11-19

**Why skip.** Every board, its embed script and anything it lists are served from one host, recruitingbypaycor.com, whose robots.txt is 'User-agent: \*' and 'Disallow: /'. The companies' own careers pages hold no listing to read instead, only a script that draws the frame from the closed host, and the nightly crawl meets the same refusal. Even open, a board could never name its employer to the crawler.

**How to spot it.** Any recruitingbypaycor.com address: find_site_boards tallies it as 'paycor'. Seen embedded as a script, \<script id="gnewtonjs" src="//recruitingbypaycor.com/career/iframe.action?clientId=\<32 hex>"> (aggregateIframe.action for a group's combined board), or linked straight to CareerHome.action?clientId=\<id>. The clientId is opaque and names nobody.

**How it publishes.** Two server-rendered pages: CareerHome.action, one employer's board, and AggregateCareerHome.action, a group's combined board, both closed. No JSON or RSS feed was seen, and none was probed for on a host closed to every crawler.

**robots.txt.** Measured 2026-11-19: recruitingbypaycor.com's robots.txt (26 bytes) is 'User-agent: \*' then 'Disallow: /', with no group for this crawler. ats.\_page refused Kahua's and Kuali's CareerHome before any page was asked, and the nightly crawl recorded the same refusal for CemSites that day.

**Where it names its employer.** States none the crawler may read: the board's own pages are closed and the clientId is an opaque id. No probe.

**Quirks.**

- Do not route around it: not through Paycor's pre-rebrand Newton host, not by guessing a feed path on the closed host, not by letting a browser run the gnewton script.
- render_fetch.only_allowed asks robots.txt for documents only, so a headless render of such a careers page aborts the Paycor frame and still downloads the gnewton script from the closed host (the research found it in passing; whether a subresource must ask is the owner's call).
- What can be done instead: hand capture, and a posts_at ruling where a company points elsewhere.

### UKG Pro Recruiting (UltiPro)

`ukg` · **skip** · no reader · no identity probe · measured 2026-11-19..2026-11-21

**Why skip.** robots.txt closes the only listing by name on every UKG host measured: Disallow: \*/JobBoardView is longer than Allow: \*/JobBoard/, so the board page's own LoadSearchResults call is refused. What it leaves open carries no full list: the board page shows an employer-chosen 'featured' subset at most, and the posting pages are open but their ids come only from the closed listing. Calling it would be working around a refusal. A person can still capture roles by hand.

**How to spot it.** Any ultipro.com, ultipro.ca or ukg.net address: find_site_boards tallies it as 'ukg'. A board is the whole triple, https://\<host>/\<TENANT>/JobBoard/\<board uuid>/, the host being recruiting[N].ultipro.com, recruiting.ultipro.ca or \<alias>.rec.pro.ukg.net; one tenant can hold several boards (Roper's tenant holds Neptune's), so the tenant alone is never the board. discover_ats.MARKERS files recruiting[N].ultipro.com/\<TENANT> as type html: the tenant root, which robots.txt closes, and it misses .ultipro.ca and rec.pro.ukg.net.

**How it publishes.** The listing is the board page's own background call, POST https://\<host>/\<TENANT>/JobBoard/\<uuid>/JobBoardView/LoadSearchResults (pageSize 50, paged by skip with a totalCount, per the page's markup; never called). The board page (437 KB to 3.5 MB) carries only a featured subset, filter facets and the tenant's job-title catalog; a posting page (OpportunityDetail?opportunityId=\<id>) is open and fully structured. No JSON-LD, RSS or sitemap.

**robots.txt.** Measured 2026-11-19..21 on recruiting.ultipro.com, recruiting2.ultipro.com, recruiting.ultipro.ca and bellhowell.rec.pro.ukg.net: the same 144-character file, User-agent: \* / Disallow: / / Allow: \*/JobBoard/ / Disallow: \*/JobBoardView / Disallow: \*/JobBoard/\*/Styles / Disallow: \*/JobBoard/\*/AnonymousSessionCheck. The listing and its filter, count and typeahead calls are refused; the board page and OpportunityDetail are allowed; the tenant root is refused.

**Where it names its employer.** Only the board's own title, jobBoard.Name on the board page, the same kind of field as Paylocity's ModuleTitle. It equalled the company's name on 2 of 7 boards (i3 Verticals, Bell and Howell); the others read like 'Honorlock Opportunities' and 'Neptune Careers'. There is no company field anywhere, and tenant aliases are codes. No probe.

**Quirks.**

- A board uuid that does not exist under a real tenant redirects to that tenant's board instead of failing, so a reader would have to check it landed on the uuid it asked.
- Parent tenants: Muni-Link's careers page links Neptune's board on Roper's tenant.
- A reader that took only the featured rows would mislead: 5 of 7 boards feature nothing, and an empty featured list proves nothing.
- welcome-us.ukg.net/u/login is UKG's employee sign-in, not a board, and the finder counts any ukg.net link as 'ukg'.

### Indeed

**How to spot it.** A link to a company's Indeed page or postings (indeed.com/cmp, /jobs or /viewjob): find_site_boards tallies it as 'indeed', where a company posts instead of keeping a board of its own.

**robots.txt.** Unknown: not measured.

### LinkedIn

`linkedin` · **seen** · no reader · no identity probe · measured 2026-10-09

**How to spot it.** A link to a company's LinkedIn jobs (linkedin.com/company/\<x>/jobs, or linkedin.com/jobs/): find_site_boards tallies it as 'linkedin', where a company posts instead of keeping a board of its own. A linkedin.com frame is never taken for a job platform (\_NOT_A_PLATFORM).

**How it publishes.** Not read, by design: scraping it would breach LinkedIn's terms. A person captures a role with the extension, and posts_at records 'linkedin' (reach: capture).

**robots.txt.** Refused: when the crawler began honouring robots.txt (2026-10-09), LinkedIn's robots.txt cost CORE Business Technologies 20 postings and Fortem Technologies 6.

**Where it names its employer.** Not a board this repository reads or wires; there is no probe.

**Quirks.**

- An advertisement is not a second board: a link to (or a mention of) the company's LinkedIn page is kept on a WIRE row as advertised_on and holds nothing (wire_found.ADVERTISED_ON).
